goal: Show-me: the hook and the compelling question, the six-step cycle card, then the teacher thinks aloud sorting questions about bats into researchable, opinion and needs data no one has yet, and rewrites one opinion question as one research can answer
note: Hook: a night photo of a bat in flight with three questions under it. Skill card "research, opinion or needs data; words, try, read the source, skip the ad, log, look back", held by the teacher; the cycle card held for this day. No readiness check: every row unit 1 assumes (g4-narrow-and-plan, g4-own-question, g4-search-more-kinds) was used in library grade 4, the year before, so each is retrieved on days 2 and 3. Rewritten questions stay on neutral things (which material, which plant), never people or groups. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): sort two new questions and rewrite one. Host: the "what is everything made of?" questions of science grade 5 unit 1 (weeks 1 to 4 in calendar.csv, in step), sorted as researchable or needing an investigation. Stand-alone: "How do bats find their way in the dark?" The bat source set says "most bats" find their way by echolocation, since many fruit bats rely mainly on sight and smell, so the sourced answer is true.

goal: Show-me: from a key-word and synonym list, the teacher changes a poor query on an invented results page (narrower, broader, a synonym, an exact phrase), reads the source name under each result, skips the marked ad, reaches the answering page inside a chosen site by its printed menu, and keeps a search log, then looks back at the log to write a next-step line
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: narrow one topic and write a plan line with a tentative answer (g4-narrow-and-plan, library grade 4). Where many miss it, the ten-minute reteach is the grade 4 move's show-me case; a class that did not take grade 4 library gets it for every student. Candidate kept: the tentative-answer cell as that plan line (about 1 minute). Minute split: retrieval 5; the key words and the four query changes, with the source names and the ad on one results page, 9; the menu case 3; the log and its look-back 7; exit ticket 5. The menu case is modeled here so day 3 only practices it. The search log sheet begun here is kept on every later inquiry day. Invented results pages name no real site; the ad is for an invented product. Stop rule on any device (g3-safe-searching): close it, tell the adult, no blame. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): change one poor query once and say why. ELA grade 5 unit 2 (e5-locate-sources, weeks 9 to 16) comes later, so this day models query changes itself.

goal: Practice: pairs with the card sort six new questions three ways and rewrite one, then fix three poor searches on invented results pages, logging each try; one case reaches the answering page by the site's printed menu
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: one question searched on two printed kinds with the same key words, saying what each gave (g4-search-more-kinds). Inside the sort, two of the six are the students' own questions: mark which research can answer (g4-own-question). Where many miss it, the ten-minute reteach is the grade 4 move's show-me case; a class that did not take grade 4 library gets it for every student. Feedback after each round. Stop rule on any device (g3-safe-searching): close it, tell the adult, no blame. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): sort three questions and fix one search.

goal: Inquiry: judge the host question, list key words, search the bat set and log each try (about 15 minutes), look back at the log and write the next-step line (about 8), then the answer found, a pair share and the self-check (about 6)
note: Card withdrawn today. Candidate kept at the judging step: one line on what I already know and what I do not, and whether the question is small enough to answer (about 2 minutes). Self-check: rate the card's steps, one thing learned, whether the answer showed its evidence, one thing to do differently. Working notes and the search log in the research notebook. Stop rule on any device (g3-safe-searching): close it, tell the adult, no blame. Whose voices: the bat set records its makers (C12).

goal: End-of-unit assessment, written sitting (about 26 minutes for 30): six new questions sorted, one opinion question rewritten and one more question research could answer written on the same topic; a poor query on a new invented results page changed twice with a reason each, source names read, the ad marked and one result reached by the printed menu; a next-step line for a new sample search log
note: New case, not seen in the unit. Sort items checked on the page (about 8 minutes); the query change and the log line on a short teacher-judged rubric (about 10 and 8 minutes). Each part of each code has its prompt: the sort and rewrite (AASL.IV.A.1), "write one more question research could answer on the same topic" after the rewrite, inside the sort's 8 minutes (~AASL.I.A.1), the next-step line (AASL.I.D.4). Searching more than one kind (~AASL.IV.B.1) is practiced on day 3, not assessed here. Taken without the card. Response time: day 6.

goal: Respond: regrouped reteach by the rubric step missed (sort and rewrite, query change, next-step line), each group ending with one fresh try; students who met every step run a second bat search and log it
note: Groups from the class record sheet (APPROACH.md, unit field 7).

goal: Show-me: the hook and the compelling question, then the teacher weighs six sources on sea turtles (print, a described video, online pages) for fit, date and reading level, writes the reason line for three, and shows a group-written encyclopedia article used as a starting map through its references
note: Hook: a photo of hatchlings heading for the sea. Skill card "fits my question, current, I can read it, why it earns its place; leave the page, who is behind it, why made, does a second source back it", held by the teacher. The encyclopedia article is an invented copy with its references. Candidate kept: the continuum's comprehensiveness cell as a "does it cover my whole question?" tick on the reason line (about 1 minute here and on days 9 and 10). Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): one reason line for a new source. Host: the rainforest research of ELA grade 5 unit 2 (e5-locate-sources, weeks 9 to 16): beside this unit from week 9; where both run, one source set may serve both. Stand-alone: "How do sea turtles find their way back to the beach where they hatched?"

goal: Show-me: before reading an unfamiliar invented page closely, the teacher leaves it, looks up the maker on the "what others say" card, decides who is behind the page and why it was made, then checks one important statement against a second supplied source and marks it supported, contradicted or not settled with a reason
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: sort three invented pages by purpose and find the ad (g4-primary-secondary). Where many miss it, the ten-minute reteach is the grade 4 move's show-me case; a class that did not take grade 4 library gets it for every student. The lateral reading model is new here: the first time library teaches leaving the page as a method. Where a school has one shared device or a projector, the teacher may show a search of the invented maker's name on a teacher-checked page; the cards do the same job in full. Stop rule on any device (g3-safe-searching): close it, tell the adult, no blame; one modeled case under it (about 1 minute): a page asks for your name and a photo, so close it and tell the adult. Bridge to health: health grade 5 unit 16 (weeks 5 to 9) runs its source check card (who made it, what they want, is there evidence, does an adult I trust agree) on invented claims the week before; the lateral check begins from its "who made it, what do they want" and adds leaving the page and checking a second source. Social studies grade 5 unit 3 (ss5-sourcing-corroboration, weeks 6 to 9) teaches sourcing on its own documents before or beside this day; library borrows only the move and never its revolution sources (K to 5 neutral rule). Leans on the online-reasoning lessons and web-literacy book, not loaded (later.csv L149). Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): one new page: who is behind it and why, from its card.

goal: Practice: pairs choose three of six sources with a reason line each, then check three invented pages laterally, one a credible-looking page with a wrong statement, marking each important statement supported, contradicted or not settled against a second supplied source
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: two poor queries for a sea turtle question changed and logged (g5-search-revise, unit 1), and one scenario card inside the same 5 minutes: a page asks for your name and a photo; what do you do? (g3-safe-searching, last used in library grade 4 and modeled on day 8). Feedback after each page. The candidate verify-the-truth cell is the lateral check's last line, kept (no time beyond the frame's). No page names a real site or organization. Leans on the unloaded online-reasoning lessons (L149). Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): one new page checked laterally with one statement marked.

goal: Inquiry: choose three sources for the host question with reason lines, check one unfamiliar page and one of its statements laterally, write a two-sentence answer with each sentence tied to its source, then a pair share of the answer and one source decision, and the self-check
note: Card withdrawn today. The search log is kept as review. Product: the two-sentence sourced answer. Self-check: rate the card's steps, one thing learned, whether the answer showed its evidence, one thing to change. Stop rule on any device (g3-safe-searching): close it, tell the adult, no blame. Whose voices: the sea turtle set records its makers (C12).

goal: End-of-unit assessment, written sitting (about 27 minutes for 30): from a new set of six, three sources chosen with a reason line each; two new invented pages, each with its card, judged for who is behind them and why before close reading, and one statement marked supported, contradicted or not settled against a second source
note: New source set (an invented one on how monarch butterflies migrate). Rubric, teacher-judged (about 12 and 15 minutes). One page in the set is the invented group-written encyclopedia, judged through its references (~AASL.IV.C.1); one item asks what the student does if a page asks for a name or a photo (~AASL.VI.A.1). Taken without the card. Response time: day 12.

goal: Respond: regrouped reteach by the rubric step missed (reason lines, who is behind the page, the statement check), each group ending with one fresh try
note: Groups from the class record sheet. The class count of each rubric step met is written on the mid-year check's sheet for day 13.

goal: Mid-year check, written sitting (about 25 minutes for 30): unit 1 on new cases, five questions sorted and one rewritten, a poor query changed twice with reasons and the ad marked, and a next-step line for a sample search log; unit 2, assessed the week before, is not re-tested
note: Week 13. Unit 2's end-of-unit result is reused unscored, as the class count on the sheet. Unit 1's forms were last given in week 5, so none repeats within two weeks. Library is a special (CALENDAR.md rule 1), and week 13 is free of grade 5 core checks.

goal: Respond: regrouped reteach on the mid-year check's missed steps and unit 2's counted steps, in small groups from the sheet, ending with one fresh try
note: Week 14.

goal: Show-me: the hook and the compelling question, then the teacher takes answer-only notes from three redwood sources on one question, marks where they agree and differ on a fact, and shows an outline and a mind map, saying which layout fits which purpose
note: Hook: a photo of a person at the foot of a redwood. Skill card "answer only, three sources, agree or differ, outline; who, what, when, where from, what kind", held by the teacher. Candidate kept: notes chosen for the purpose and an outline or mind map (now in the row note), modeled here (about 4 minutes) and chosen with a reason on days 17 and 18. Differences are factual only (a height, an age, a count), never views (K to 5 neutral rule); the heights and ages are invented for practice or carry their free source and an as-of date. Whole numbers compared only. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): mark one agreement in two short notes. Host: ELA grade 5 unit 2's rainforest research (e5-research, weeks 9 to 16) ends in this unit's second week, so its notes are already in hand; science grade 5 unit 5's water question runs weeks 21 to 25, after this unit, so it is not in step. Stand-alone: "How tall do redwood trees grow, and how old can they get?"

goal: Show-me: the teacher builds a bibliography to the model for a book, a described video and a web page (author, title, date, publisher or site, kind of source) and thinks aloud on why a page with no maker is a weak source
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: two answer-only notes from a short paragraph (g4-evidence-notes). Where many miss it, the ten-minute reteach is the grade 4 move's show-me case; a class that did not take grade 4 library gets it for every student. Candidate dropped: the credit-with-page-number cell, because the frame's Check set read places page numbers in a credit in grades 6 to 8. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): one bibliography entry for a new source.

goal: Practice: mark agreement and difference in three short passages and pick a layout with a one-line reason, put five sources into a bibliography, and correct two faulty entries to the model
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: fix one not-yet-honest case (g4-honest-use). Where many miss it, the ten-minute reteach is the grade 4 move's show-me case; a class that did not take grade 4 library gets it for every student. Feedback after each part. Honest use without shaming: a copied sentence is fixed with the student privately. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): one difference marked and one entry corrected.

goal: Inquiry: notes from three sources for the host question with the agree and differ marks, an outline or mind map chosen with a one-line reason, a brief answer saying what the sources agree on, what still differs and which evidence backs it, a bibliography, a pair share and the self-check
note: Card withdrawn today. Any unfamiliar page in the set is checked laterally first, as review. Product: the brief answer with its bibliography. Self-check: rate the card's steps, one thing learned, whether the answer showed its evidence, one thing to change. Whose voices: the redwood set records its makers (C12).

goal: End-of-unit assessment, written sitting (about 25 minutes for 30): three new short passages on one question, answer-only notes with each agreement and difference marked, and a line saying which plan the notes are sorted by and why; a bibliography for three new sources (a book, a described video, a web page with no maker) and one line on why the unnamed page is weak
note: New case (an invented set on how long giant tortoises live). Rubric, teacher-judged (about 13 and 12 minutes). Each part has its prompt: notes that answer (~AASL.I.B.1), "say which plan your notes are sorted by and why", inside the 13-minute notes part (~AASL.IV.B.4), the agree and differ marks (facts only; comparing views, ~AASL.II.B.2, is begun on days 15, 17 and 18 and not assessed here), the entries (~AASL.VI.B.2) and the unnamed-page line (~AASL.VI.A.2). Taken without the card. Response time: day 20.

goal: Respond: regrouped reteach by the rubric step missed (answer-only notes, the marks, bibliography entries), each group ending with one fresh try
note: Groups from the class record sheet.

goal: Show-me: the hook and the compelling question, then the teacher splits a wetland question into subquestions, pools sample findings on the pooling sheet, says how the question grew, and chooses a real audience and a form for it
note: Hook: a photo of a wetland beside a stream. Skill card "split, research, bring back, pool, how did it grow; who cares, what form, answer their questions", held by the teacher. Groups of three, mixed by the teacher, never by background. Audience on the classroom route: a younger class, families at a school display or the school office. ELA grade 5 unit 3 (e5-presenting, weeks 17 to 25) is before or beside; this day models choosing a form for an audience itself, and the spoken delivery is ELA's. Exit ticket (about 5 minutes, all at once): split a new question into three subquestions. Host: science grade 5 unit 6, protecting water by design (s5-protect-resources), runs weeks 25 to 30, so it meets only days 25 to 27; the research days run on the stand-alone wetland question (the frame's "if later" line), and science unit 5 (weeks 21 to 25) is in step for the water background. Kept to how water is kept clean, never a local dispute or who is to blame. Stand-alone: "How do wetlands clean water, and who in our school should know?"

goal: Inquiry: each member researches a subquestion with the year's moves (a logged search, a lateral check on any unfamiliar page, answer-only notes, bibliography entries) and brings back findings
note: Opens with the five-minute retrieval task: say which subquestion a class survey could answer (g4-class-survey) and rewrite one closed question as open (g4-asking-others). Where many miss it, the ten-minute reteach is the grade 4 move's show-me case; a class that did not take grade 4 library gets it for every student. At home, the teaching adult researches a second subquestion for the pooling step. Stop rule on any device (g3-safe-searching): close it, tell the adult, no blame.
retrieves: g4-class-survey; g4-asking-others; g5-search-revise; g5-search-log-look-back; g5-first-lateral-check; g5-evidence-notes

goal: Inquiry: groups pool their findings on the pooling sheet, write how the question grew, and choose the form for their audience
note: Candidate kept at the pooling: each member hears another's finding and says it back before the group pools (the continuum's working-together and listening cells, about 3 minutes).

goal: Inquiry: groups draft the product and its bibliography from the pooling sheet on the short product template, each member's part marked
note: Product on paper or a display board. Honest use without shaming: a copied sentence is fixed with the student privately.

goal: Inquiry: revise the product from advice; groups take teacher and peer advice, revise the product, keep a change log, and list the audience's likely questions with answers from the research
note: Opens with the retrieval inside the revision: one change-log line for a piece of advice (g4-revise-from-advice). Where many miss it, the ten-minute reteach is the grade 4 move's show-me case; a class that did not take grade 4 library gets it for every student. A revision from advice before the product is scored, so an inquiry day (GLOSSARY: drafting and revising are Application), not a respond day; unit 4's response time is day 29 alone.

goal: Share with the real audience and score it: each group presents for about 90 seconds and takes brief questions (about 20 minutes in all), every student presenting one source-backed part; the product is scored on its rubric and each student's sharing result recorded beside it; then the self-check
note: Part one of the end-of-unit assessment. Rubric: the form fits the audience, the findings and evidence are clear (candidate kept: presenting so the evidence reaches the audience, a rubric line, no time), the audience's questions answered from the research; the product reflects the revision (~AASL.I.C.3) and is a made product (~AASL.I.B.3). Audience questions may be answered jointly, with contributions named; no student is asked about home. At home the student presents their own sourced part to the teaching adult and answers one question; the same individual criteria apply. Families see a display at pickup or a school event, never as a required visit. Self-check: rate the card's steps, one thing learned, whether the product showed its evidence, one thing to change.

goal: End-of-unit assessment, written sitting (about 20 minutes for 30): each student explains what researching with the group added and how the question grew, and chooses and justifies a form for a new audience card
note: Part two of the end-of-unit assessment (about 12 and 8 minutes, rubric). It reuses day 26's sharing record and does not collect it again. One item asks where a subquestion needed a survey rather than a source (~AASL.V.C.2). Response time: day 29 alone (12 minutes of regrouped reteach).

goal: Year-end check, written sitting (about 27 minutes for 30): units 1 to 3 on new cases, a smaller sample than the units' own sittings: one question judged and one query changed, one source chosen from three with its reason and one page checked laterally with one statement marked, notes from two brief passages with an agreement and a difference marked and one bibliography entry; unit 4, assessed the week before, is not re-tested
skills: g5-research-or-guess; g5-search-revise; g5-choose-sources; g5-first-lateral-check; g5-evidence-notes; g5-bibliography
note: Week 28. Minutes: about 5, 8 and 12, plus about 2 to reread and finish (provisional until the pages are tried). Unit 4's result is reused unscored as a class count on the sheet. Forms last given in weeks 11, 13 and 19, so none repeats within two weeks. Lateral item leans on the unloaded online-reasoning lessons (L149).

note: Week 29. Groups from the class record sheet and the check's sheet.
